title: Service account onboarding flow: enforced templates, delegated ownership, and approval hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Teams frequently create long-lived service accounts without clear owners or scopes. This results in orphaned principals, over-permissive roles, and noisy audit trails. Goal: Provide a self-serve, auditable onboarding flow for service accounts that enforces least-privilege templates, captures ownership metadata, and integrates optional approval hooks for sensitive templates. Deliverables: 1) UI/CLI flow for creating service accounts with a required template selector and owner field (owner may be a user or team). 2) A small template library (JSON templates) with parameterized scopes (read-only, write-limited, admin-lite). 3) Automated ownership assignment rules: if the creator is not in the org directory, require explicit owner selection; if owner is a group, capture group id. 4) Approval webhook for templates flagged as "elevated" that sends to the approvals service (and blocks creation until approved). 5) Audit log entries for creation, owner changes, template used, and approval decisions (structured fields for downstream analytics). 6) Migration script to detect existing service accounts lacking owner or template metadata and open remediation tasks in a report. Non-goals: User-facing personal API keys; rotating key material (separate lifecycle epic). Implementation notes: - Backend: extend service_accounts table with columns: template_id, owner_principal, owner_type, elevated_flag, created_via (UI/CLI/API). Add DB migration and backfill job (see attachments). - API: new /v2/service-accounts endpoint with stricter schema validation and an optional approval_token header for approved elevated templates. - UI: creation modal updated with template preview, policy hints, and a required owner selector with directory lookup. - Approval flow: call /approvals/v1/request with template snapshot; approval outcome stored in audit log. - Audit: Emit structured events to the audit pipeline (topic: audit.service_accounts) with fields: actor, action, template_id, owner, approval_id, request_id, timestamp. - Tests: unit tests for validation, integration tests for approval flow, e2e that simulates orphaned account migration. Acceptance criteria: - New accounts created via the new flow must have owner and template_id set in DB. - Elevated template creations must be blocked until approvals service returns approved. - Backfill job identifies >95% of orphaned accounts and creates remediation tasks. - Audit events for create/update must contain template_id and owner fields. Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag behind rbacs.ASOnboard.ui and rbacs.ASOnboard.api. 2) Beta to internal teams for 2 weeks, gather feedback. 3) Open telemetry/backfill runs in parallel. 4) Gradual enable for all orgs with monitoring dashboards for orphan rate, approval latency, and failed create attempts. Migration and cleanup: - Backfill scan (batch job) to tag existing accounts missing template_id. - For accounts with stale or absent owner, create remediation tickets assigned to original creator where available; otherwise assign to security-oncall. - After 90 days of remediation window, auto-rotate keys and notify owners (policy requirement). Security considerations: - Ensure approval payloads do not leak secret material. - Template schema validated against allowed actions; disallow wildcard resources. - Audit logs must be immutable and retained per compliance policy. - Integrate with SSO directory to resolve owners and group membership. Open questions: - Do we need per-tenant custom templates or will a global library suffice? (Product asks for multi-tenant templates; implementation will scope templates by org_id.) - Should owner be allowed to be a service account? (Currently disallow; may allow delegated ownership with an explicit skip flag and stronger approval.)
acceptance_criteria: All new service accounts created through the new UI/API include non-empty owner and template_id fields in DB
Elevated templates require an approval and cannot be created without an approval_token
Backfill job identifies >95% of service accounts without owner/template metadata and surfaces remediation tasks
Audit event schema includes actor, action, template_id, owner, approval_id and is published to audit.service_accounts
